_comment: Team template (team config, schema 1) → product/<team>/team.json. Step T0: draft it with python3 scripts/new_team.py --init <team> --field "..." --members "Name One;Name Two;Name Three", complete it by hand following these notes, then run python3 scripts/new_team.py product/<team>/team.json, which scaffolds the team from it and the templates in this folder; every later workflow and script (team_status.py, the scripts/workflows/*.js runs) reads it.

All values below are fictional placeholders (the same fictional team, product/example-team, that scripts/workflows/examples/ uses for dry runs; its first two members are the dry-run members). Real team.json files carry no _comment key. See product/dfo-team for a worked example (team.json).
schema: always 1. team: folder name under product/ (lowercase, hyphenated). title: display name used in the README, the roundtable and the triggers.
field: the field and the tradition within it that the team covers; name the neighbouring traditions that are not represented.
language: language of the member skills and their paper cards (cards for a researcher who writes in English are written in English).
created: ISO date of T0. roundtable: slug of the roundtable skill folder inside the team folder.
chase_hints (team level): field-wide legitimate open-access repositories that team-chase.js searches first (preprint servers, open proceedings, report series).

card_dimensions (optional): what the paper-card dimensions D1–D8 mean in this field when it is not mathematical or computational, e.g. {"D3": "sources and archives: what evidence the argument rests on", "D4": "the interpretive or analytical moves", "D5": "how claims are tested against counter-evidence"}. Every read agent (team-read.js, team-increment.js) uses these meanings; digest field names stay the same. Leave it {} for mathematical and computational fields.

source_labels (optional): {"<keyword in a work's URL>": "<Source label>"} for full texts supplied by hand from a known report series, e.g. {"damtp": "DAMTP report"}; acquire_fulltexts.py writes the label into INDEX.md's Source column instead of "manual".

members: the researchers this team distills itself (at least one); together with any guests (see below), 3-6 seated researchers chosen for complementary lenses and documented disagreements. Per member:

slug: skill folder name (lowercase, hyphenated full name). name: display name. surname: used for lens labels (@Surname, [Surname lens], add/drop Surname), so it must be unique within the team: when two members share a surname, write e.g. "N. Higham" and "D. Higham". family_name (optional): the family name used in author checks and searches when the last word of name is not it (e.g. a name written family-name first); defaults to that last word.
living: false marks a historical lens (its skill reflects work up to the researcher's death).
hint: one line that disambiguates the researcher in searches (institutions, years, signature work).

scholar: Google Scholar user id (the user= value in the profile URL), or empty if there is none: the harvest then searches Scholar by name once and otherwise builds the list from DBLP and the homepage (find the DBLP pid with python3 scripts/dblp_works.py --name "<name>"). dblp: DBLP pid if known. orcid, homepage: empty if unknown. python3 scripts/new_team.py product/<team>/team.json --lookup fills dblp / orcid / homepage from DBLP (a Scholar-link match is certain; a name-only match is flagged for checking), and --set-member <slug> KEY=VALUE records a value, e.g. the Scholar id the harvest found.
chase_hints: member-specific open sources (institutional report series, homepage paper pages), with any access quirks (e.g. a host that only works over http).
student_mode: true gives the skill a Student Mode plus references/proof-playbook.md, open-problems.md and reading-path.md.

guests (optional): members of other teams seated in this team's roundtable and README, with no second copy of their skills (a guest's folder is never copied, linked or scaffolded here). A list of {"slug": "<the member's slug in its home team>", "home": "<the home team's folder under product/>"}, e.g. "guests": [{"slug": "cy-sample", "home": "home-example-team"}] (fictional; this example has no live guests key, because that home team does not exist and the entry would fail resolution).

rules: exactly the keys slug and home. slug is unique within guests and differs from every member slug, from roundtable and from lead (if any); home is a folder name like team, never this team and never a team that guest_teams (whole teams seated, as in product/optimization-council) already seats. new_team.py and team_check.py resolve each guest: product/<home>/team.json lists the slug under members (a guest of a guest is not allowed: seat it from its home team), product/<home>/<slug>/ exists (else run the home team's --add-member first), and this team has no folder of that name. A person is a member of one team and can be a guest in others; members here stays non-empty, and members plus guests make the 3-6 seats. Surnames are compared across members and guests: on a clash, rename this team's member (two guests: rename it in one guest's home team.json).

from the home team: name, surname, family_name, living, hint, the ids and student_mode are read from the home entry verbatim and edited there (a key missing there, e.g. living, stays missing: never add it here). The guest's T1, T3, T4, --lookup and --set-member run in its home team, whose tier, language, card_dimensions and chase_hints apply to it; this team's scripts and workflows read its folder and never write it. Draft with new_team.py --init <team> ... --guests "home/slug;home/slug", or add the entries by hand; then scaffold as usual with python3 scripts/new_team.py product/<team>/team.json, which gives each guest a row in the README and the roundtable and no folder. On a team that is already scaffolded, add the entry and run python3 scripts/new_team.py product/<team>/team.json --add-guest <slug> (it adds the README row only); python3 scripts/new_team.py product/<team>/team.json --guest-text prints, read-only, the exact guest sentences and rows the README, the roundtable and DEEP-READING.md should carry, which the team layer (T2) and team-integrate.js (T3.8) check against. The team layer (T2) waits until every guest has a SKILL.md on this branch: merge the home team's branch first (steps in references/research-team-playbook.md, section 八).
